purpose: Hand-authored claims of which theories/<Module>.v are checked, by a differential or extraction-based test, against the ACTUAL shipped production OCaml — not merely against the extracted Rocq model compared to itself, or against a hand-written mirror. This is a distinct question from 'is it proven': every theorem in proof-ledger.json is proven either way. It is the backlog-201 answer to 'model vs production' for this project, made mechanical rather than left to README prose. scripts/check-production-link.py verifies each entry below against the freshly generated ledger (the module must exist and have the theorem count claimed) and the named test file's real content (production_call must appear as a live call, comments stripped — a stale claim whose test regressed must fail, not silently keep being cited).

PtxLayout.note: extraction/LayoutExtract.v extracts PtxLayout.v to OCaml; test_layout_conformance.ml runs those extracted definitions directly against Sarek_ir_layout for accept/reject and every offset/size: EXHAUSTIVELY over every record shape with 1-4 fields and every variant shape with 1-3 constructors of 0-2 args (780 + 30783 shapes), plus 500 seeded random deeper cases and host/mixed-alignment pins (11 Alcotest cases total). scripts/check-formal-proofs.sh re-extracts from scratch and byte-compares against the committed extraction on every run, so this link cannot drift silently. 'exhaustive' is bounded (<=4 fields / <=3 ctors x <=2 args) plus randomised beyond that bound, not exhaustive over all possible layouts.
